author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A vessel moving through the Strait of Hormuz was reportedly struck by a projectile early Sunday, according to the British navy-linked United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency. UKMTO said the extent of any damage and the condition of the crew were not immediately known, leaving the incident under active assessment.

The report arrived one day after Saudi Arabia temporarily closed its East-West oil pipeline following a drone attack. That 1,200-kilometer route has carried roughly 4 million to 5 million barrels per day while wartime disruption has sharply reduced traffic through Hormuz. Saudi officials said injuries and damage from the pipeline strike were still being assessed.

No immediate claim of responsibility was reported for the vessel incident. The latest alert adds pressure to two strategically important energy corridors at once: Hormuz at the entrance to the Gulf and the Red Sea route served by the Saudi pipeline. Shipping operators and governments were awaiting verified information about the vessel, its crew and any effect on traffic.
dek: A British maritime agency said damage and crew conditions were unknown as energy-route security concerns intensified early Sunday.
headline: Projectile reportedly hits vessel in Strait of Hormuz
